result.headline: Rays depth 4 lifts DQN's test score to 26.7 from 21.3 for the short-vision baseline, but depth 9 adds nothing, and the GA's score is held back by looping: 34 of its 100 test games ended by starving.
result.summary:
**GA (neuroevolution, a population of networks that breed and mutate):** test mean 28.62 on seed 0, with median 28 and best game 44. Across the three seeds it averages 32.64 (std 3.76; values 28.62, 33.23, 36.07). Its training curve climbs quickly, from 12.2 at 0.44 min to 30.0 at 3.9 min, then flattens near 30-31 for the last six minutes. That is the elite line the GA keeps. The full generation's mean (population_mean) rises from 4.2 to about 27, so the children are still improving. In 10 minutes it ran 79.6M env steps at about 130k steps per second.

**DQN (Deep Q-learning, which learns the value of each move from stored experience):** test mean 26.69 on seed 0 and 26.57 across seeds (std 1.39). Its training mean sits at 19-21 after the first minute. That is lower than the test score because exploration moves are included. It ran only 1.2M env steps at about 2k steps per second, so it is roughly 66 times slower per step than the GA.

**How the games ended:** the GA's seed-0 games took 1,372 steps and 48 steps per apple, and 34 games ended by starving (looping without eating). Its other seeds starved far less (11 and 3 games). DQN games are short, at 237 steps and 9 steps per apple, and end by crashing, about half into walls and half into its own body. It never starves.
result.diagnosis:
The depth change itself is clear. Compared with the short-vision baseline, DQN gained about 5 points (21.31 to 26.69) under the same reward and settings. That baseline is only one seed, though, and the three depth-4 seeds spread by 1.4, so this is a probable gain, not a settled one. Going from depth 4 to depth 9 changed nothing: GA 32.64 vs 29.34 and DQN 26.57 vs 26.75, with overlapping spreads. Most of the GA's apparent gap is its reward. The baseline GA used a survival bonus (0.1 per move) and an apple reward of 100, so its 51.55 is not comparable with this run.

The GA's starving is a reward problem. Its reward is only apples and deaths, so a snake that loops forever without dying pays nothing for wasting time. Starving is not penalised, and some seeds drift into loops. DQN's crashes are a different problem. With gamma 0.95 it values only about the next 20 moves, which is probably too short to see a body trap coming. Its speed (about 2k steps per second) also limits how much it can learn in 10 minutes.
result.learned: Seeing further helped the DQN here, but the bigger effects came from the reward and the training horizon. Judge any change against the spread across seeds, and check how the games ended before deciding why a score moved.

recommendations.title: Penalise starving to stop GA looping
recommendations.why: The GA's seed-0 test games ended by starving in 34 of 100 cases, and its steps per apple were 48. Starvation is currently unpunished, so looping costs nothing.
recommendations.change: Add a starve penalty of 10 to the reward, keeping apple 10 and death 10.
recommendations.prediction: GA starved games fall from 34 to under 5 out of 100, steps per game drop below 600, and the test mean rises above 32. An earlier run with the same penalty reached 33.95. DQN should barely move (within about 1.4).
recommendations.question: Does penalising starvation cut the GA's looping and raise its test score?

recommendations.title: Raise DQN gamma to 0.99
recommendations.why: DQN crashes into walls and its own body with a 20-move planning horizon at gamma 0.95. Looking further ahead in time may help it avoid traps. This is a different kind of looking further from the lesson's spatial question.
recommendations.change: Set the DQN's gamma to 0.99 and leave everything else as it is.
recommendations.prediction: DQN test mean rises from 26.6 to about 28-30, and its games get longer than 237 steps. The GA is unchanged.
recommendations.question: Does valuing the future more reduce DQN's early crashes?

recommendations.title: Test rays depth 1 as a control
recommendations.why: Depth 4 and depth 9 scored about the same, so the real question is whether depth 4 beats depth 1 under this same reward. The short-vision baseline used a different encoding, so this run provides a cleaner control.
recommendations.change: Set the rays depth to 1 and keep everything else as it is.
recommendations.prediction: DQN drops by about 2-5 points from 26.6 to about 22-25, and GA also falls. If depth 1 scores close to depth 4, seeing further is not what helped.
recommendations.question: Does seeing 4 squares ahead beat seeing only 1 square ahead, with the reward held fixed?

ideas.title: Plot learning curves against env steps
ideas.what: Add a view that plots each algorithm's test or training score against env steps as well as wall-clock minutes, so sample efficiency can be seen directly.
ideas.why: The GA took about 80M env steps in 10 minutes and DQN about 1.2M. Under equal wall-clock time the comparison hides how much more per step DQN learns.
ideas.expected: Makes the sample-efficiency gap visible at a glance. Teaching value rather than a score change.
